clue.text: Country hoarding gold, all there is to see?

indicators.note: a country hoarding something keeps it stored within, so the gold goes inside

parts.note: Panama is a Central American country
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A country stockpiling its gold reserves, perhaps impressive to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide unbroken view takes in the whole scene, everything visible from one spot; the question mark flags the playful phrasing.

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A modest retiree performing ballet in a tutu, to comic effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone humble is modest and makes no showy claims about status.

indicators.note: the chosen letter goes in, entering the sauce

parts.note: pesto is an Italian basil sauce

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of Finger

explanation.surface: Someone dips a finger into a sauce in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tempo marking meaning at speed, and more loosely a magician's word for instantly.

definitions.meaning: to sieve or filter liquid off solids
a variety or breed within a species, such as a virus type

explanation.surface: Splitting off an identifiable faction from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for filtering through a sieve, and also for a distinct variety of plant, animal or microbe.

clue.text: Bird touring Spain mistaken for dog

indicators.note: the bird goes all round the other letters, as one touring a country travels round it

parts.note: a cockerel is a young male chicken

indicators.note: a mistaken word is wrongly put together, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller in Spain confuses a bird with a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of gun dog with long ears, an example of the general category.

indicators.note: the answer is tucked inside the run of letters spanning these two words

explanation.surface: A greedy giant eats a burrito with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' reads as eating, but it signals letters lodged across the end of burrito and the start of greedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale monster of huge size, so giant serves as a synonym.

indicators.note: we hear tells you the word for house is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a manor is a country house

explanation.surface: Gossip about a fashion house, passed on as hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion house' looks like one phrase, a couture firm, but it splits: Fashion is the definition and house the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashion as a noun can mean a way or style of doing something, as in 'in this fashion'.

indicators.note: one letter is included within the other word

parts.note: tough means hard or difficult
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Despite the hardship, a hospital stay was part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of concession used to qualify a preceding statement, so one swaps for the other.

clue.text: Guffaw unrefined, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: signals that the word for unrefined is matched by sound, in British non-rhotic speech

parts.note: raw materials are unrefined or unprocessed

explanation.surface: A coarse belly laugh, judging by how it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The pairing relies on a British accent where the final R is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud hearty laugh can be described as a roar, as in roaring with laughter.

clue.text: Inside winter vehicle, poor journalist tied up

indicators.note: Inside tells you the journalist goes within the vehicle

parts.note: a sled is a sledge pulled over snow
a hack is a low-grade writer

explanation.surface: A struggling reporter is found bound up inside a snow sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Fettered with chains or bonds, hence restrained or tied up.

parts.note: a snake casts or sheds its skin
down is soft fine plumage

explanation.surface: A bird gloomy at moulting its plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal adjective for dejected or downcast, a synonym of unhappy.

clue.text: Success that may rise or fall

definitions.text: Success that may rise or fall

indicators.note: in a down light the word reads identically going upwards or downwards

parts.note: an exclamation used as a noun for a sensational hit

explanation.surface: A hit whose fortunes might go up or down.
explanation.walkthrough: The rise-or-fall wording looks like fortunes changing; it means the three letters read the same up the grid as down.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a sensational hit can be called this, as in 'the show was a real smash'.

indicators.note: drop the opening letter of the word for trash

parts.note: tripe means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Instruction to prepare by clearing out the rubbish first.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit at its peak is ready to eat, and plans can be ready or mature.

parts.note: in golf the pin is the flagstick marking the hole
the point of an action is its aim or goal

explanation.surface: Recognising a flag and target, as on a golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf, the pin is the flagstick standing in the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate or single out something precisely, a verb synonym of identify.

explanation.surface: A loaf from France that causes misery.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for bread is spelt the same as the English word for hurt or distress.

indicators.note: the head of the word school is its opening letter

parts.note: weeping means crying from distress

explanation.surface: The headteacher of a state secondary school breaks down in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school, which makes 'Comprehensive school's head' look like one phrase; the definition is the adjective alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping changes are wide-ranging and all-embracing, so the adjectives are synonyms.

indicators.note: something juddering shakes violently, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Excavators went by, shaking as they passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden tools used to dig the ground, the plural of a basic digging implement.

clue.text: Tip I have cut for salad plant

parts.note: an end or tip of something
I have, cut short, is the contraction with an apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone advising they've trimmed a leaf for the salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy chicory plant whose bitter leaves are eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Ultimately jubilant welcome with Asian country

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of jubilant

parts.note: to hail someone is to greet or welcome them
and means together with

explanation.surface: A joyful greeting from an Asian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Southeast Asian kingdom formerly called Siam, so a specific example of the category.

clue.text: Pay attention, River Humber's opening up

indicators.note: the opening of Humber is its first letter
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A warning to watch as the Humber estuary widens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is an estuary in northeast England; 'River Humber' looks like one name but River is DEE, turned upwards to give EED.
explanation.definitionFit: To take notice of or mind something, a verb synonym of listen carefully.

indicators.note: short means the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: not a soul means nobody at all

explanation.surface: Twelve people, but nobody at all, a little under.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, the hour at which the sun is highest.

clue.text: Before end of sale, object reserved

indicators.note: Before puts the objection ahead of the following letter

parts.note: to demur is to raise an objection

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of sale

explanation.surface: Raising a complaint just before the sales close, about something already set aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' suggests an item held at a sale, but it is the definition meaning shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest and quiet in manner, so a synonym of shy and reticent.

clue.text: Battle with ninjas oddly in European city

parts.note: to vie is to compete or battle

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of ninjas

explanation.surface: A fight with ninjas, oddly taking place in a European capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian capital on the Danube, an example of a European city.
